subject: ACME private GPU pool: tail-latency hedging & provisioning pulse
messages:
From: Alex Chen <ops@acme-systems.com>

Date: 2026-10-04T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Initial sizing ask: ACME private GPU pool throughput shapes

Mateo / team,

Thanks for taking this on. We're starting to plan a VPC deployment for ACME's internal inference workloads (customer-facing search + summarization) and need a capacity recommendation and a short runbook for tail-latency hedging. High-level notes:

- Expected steady-state: ~2,500 qps (requests/sec) across a mix of short chat and longer summarization prompts.
- Burst windows: 10–15x peak for 3–10 minute windows (e.g., feature launches).
- Target p95 latency goal: <120ms; p99 target: <400ms for chat flows. For long summarization we accept p95 ~350ms.
- KV cache hit expected ~40% after warmup; prefix caching possible for 30% of requests.
- Data plane in us-west; private VPC with dedicated GPU pool behind a NAT/peering attachment.

Can you provide:
1) Ballpark GPU count (type-agnostic) and headroom target for steady vs burst.
2) Network egress and internal throughput estimates (Gbps) for the pool.
3) Suggested admission-control tiers and warm-pool sizing for meeting the p99 SLA during bursts.
4) Any procurement timeline constraints we should flag for ACME's procurement team.

I've attached our sampled q3 traffic shape and an internal requirements memo.

Regards,
Alex
Ops, ACME Systems

Attachments: acme_traffic_patterns_q3.csv (CSV), acme_initial_mlp_requirements.pdf (PDF)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask: ACME private GPU pool throughput shapes

Alex — thanks for the clear brief and the attachments. Quick read-through produces a few clarifying Qs but below is a pragmatic first-pass that we can refine during a call: 

Summary answers (ballpark):
1) GPU estimate: For your mixed workload I would recommend starting with a 16–24 GPU pool (A100/80GB equiv) as the steady committed slab to meet sustained qps with ~2x oversubscription headroom for typical batching. Set an on-demand burst pool that can add another 40–60 GPUs for short windows.

2) Network: Plan for ~28–45 Gbps egress to support the burst headroom (assumes average token sizes and 40% KV cache). Steady-state egress ~6–9 Gbps. Internal RDMA/host NIC planning should assume 100Gbps uplinks per rack with appropriate NIC oversubscription control.

3) Admission and warm-pool: Define three SLA classes: standard (p95<120, p99<400), priority (p95<80, p99<250), and background (best effort for batch summarization). Warm pool sized to be ~10–15% of burst GPUs (i.e., keep 6–9 GPUs warm) to reduce cold-start tail spikes. Also recommend active KV cache pre-warming for top 30 intent prefixes before expected launches.

4) Procurement cadence: If you need commit pricing for Dedicated/reserved capacity, procurement lead-time is ~6–8 weeks for hardware and contractual alignment, plus another 2–3 weeks for network peering and security onboarding.

Next steps: Proposed 45-minute sync with infra + procurement tomorrow to agree on exact GPU families and on-prem timeline. Karthik — please pull a quick per-GPU QPS estimate and p99 delta assumptions based on current serving kernel optimizations; Grace/Laura, flag procurement and SLA packaging constraints.

Thanks,
Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask: ACME private GPU pool throughput shapes — quick calc

Folks — did a quick back-of-envelope with current perf profiles (A100-like kernel stack, quantized 4-bit medium prompts):

Assumptions:
- Average chat request token generation: 40 tokens/output; inference cost ~0.35 TFLOP-per-token equivalent for your model profile.
- Summarization flows average 220 tokens output; cost ~1.8x chat per request.
- Per-GPU sustained token throughput w/ batching: ~3500 tokens/s (conservative). Peak-burst achievable with temp batching/continuous-batcher tweaks: ~9k tokens/s per GPU for short windows.

Steady math:
- Steady 2,500 qps (mix weighted): approx 2,500 * (avg tokens per request 80) = 200k tokens/s total.
- At 3.5k tokens/s per GPU => ~58 GPUs to meet steady if no batching or cache. But with 40% KV cache & prefix cached 30% of requests effective token load drops ~52% => effective tokens/s ~96k -> ~28 GPUs.

Burst window (10x traffic):
- 10x effective tokens/s -> 960k tokens/s. At burst per-GPU 9k tokens/s => ~107 GPUs. Accounting for headroom and safety -> provision burst cap ~120 GPUs.

Network egress check:
- Avg token serialised size ~50 bytes (post-compression). At steady tokens/s 96k -> ~4.8 MB/s ~38 Mbps (this seems low because of headers and payloads) — realistic planning uses 15–25x overhead for transport and parallel connections -> plan steady 6–9 Gbps. Burst ~30–45 Gbps.

Recommendations (concrete):
- Initial committed slab: 32 GPUs (to get comfortable on SLAs while negotiating).
- Warm-burst pool: keep 12 GPUs warm; on-demand scale to 120 for launches (use pre-warmed snapshots / OCI images to cut provisioning time to sub-90s for containers).
- Admission controls: token-based concurrency cap by SLA class + global token budget. Drop-to-background behaviour should be tested.
- Telemetry: add a burst-run counter metric and p99-slo-breach per-tenant alarm routed to teams.

I'll attach a short calc sheet to the Drive link.

-karthik
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — important procurement/ops bits to call out before we finalize: 

- Pricing model: For Dedicated/reserved we can offer a base-commit with a burst credit pool billed per-minute at a premium rate. Need to confirm ACME's expected monthly committed hours to give an accurate blended unit price.
- SLA packaging: For the priority SLA (p99<250ms) we need a 90-day traffic history baseline and a signed runbook addendum that allows emergency scale-outs during launch windows. Legal wants an explicit clause for burst-related overage caps.
- Timeline: If ACME needs contract signature + dedicated pool by Dec 1, procurement wants the exact GPU family specified and network peering IP ranges by Oct 20. That's about 6 weeks to order and stage.

Action items:
1) Mateo/Karthik — confirm proposed committed GPUs (we have tentative 32) and warm-pool sizing (12).
2) Mateo — draft runbook addendum for emergency scale-out and warm-pool charges, include expected provisioning times (warm container snapshot start ~45–90s).
3) Laura — coordinate with ACME procurement to capture monthly committed hours and calendar constraints; Laura, please include vendor onboarding checklist.

Grace
Director, Customer Ops — Redwood Inference

All — thanks for the fast turn. Finalizing items on my side: 

- Committed slab recommendation: 32 GPUs (A100/80GB equiv) with signed 6-month commit.
- Burst plan: Warm 12 GPUs + on-demand to 120 GPUs using pre-warmed snapshots and container layering; expected cold-to-warm ~45–90s depending on image delta.
- Admission policy: implement SLA classes with token-budget enforcement + background drop to best-effort for summarization when budget exhausted.
- Network: request ACME to allocate 100Gbps rack uplinks and provide peering prefixes by 2026-10-19. We'll provision 40Gbps NAT/egress aggregates initially and tune.

Deliverables by EOD 2026-10-06:
- Mateo: runbook addendum draft + per-minute overage pricing sample
- Karthik: attach calc sheet and per-GPU test profile
- Laura: draft vendor onboarding checklist for ACME procurement
